title: Inverse trig functions
examples: What is the range of the inverse cosine function?
How do I graph the inverse tangent function?
Does the domain of arcsin match the range of sin?

explain.say: Today we look at inverse trig functions. These functions undo the actions of the regular trig functions. For example, sin and arcsin are inverses of each other. The function arcsin asks for an angle, not a ratio.
Because trig functions repeat, we must restrict their domain to make them invertible. This restricted range gives us the principal value. The principal value is the main answer we use.
For arcsin, the principal value range is negative pi divided by two to pi divided by two. This means the angle is between negative ninety and ninety degrees. The domain remains negative one to one.

Let us look at a concrete example. If you calculate arcsin of one divided by two, the answer is pi divided by six. This is because sin of pi divided by six is indeed one divided by two. Remember the principal value rule.

faq.q: What is the domain for the inverse sine function?
faq.a: The domain for arcsin is negative one to one. This is because the sine function's output values are always between negative one and one. You might also ask what values can I put into arcsin?
asks: What is the input for arcsin?
What values are in the domain of arcsin?

faq.q: What is the range for the inverse cosine function?
faq.a: The principal value range for arccos is zero to pi. This restriction keeps the function one-to-one. Another way to ask this is what is the output angle for arccos?
asks: What are the possible angles from arccos?
What is the range of arccos?

faq.q: Do all inverse trig functions have the same range?
faq.a: No, each function has its own specific principal value range. For instance, arctan has a range of negative pi divided by two to pi divided by two. You could also ask about the range differences.
asks: Are the ranges always the same?
What is the range difference between the inverses?

faq.q: Why do we need to restrict the domain?
faq.a: We restrict the domain because the original trig functions are periodic. A periodic function fails the horizontal line test, so it is not one-to-one. This restriction creates the inverse function.
asks: Why can't we use the whole graph?

faq.q: How do I graph the inverse tangent function?
faq.a: The graph of arctan has horizontal asymptotes at negative pi divided by two and pi divided by two. It passes through the origin point. You might also ask about the asymptotes of arctan.
asks: What are the asymptotes for arctan?
How does the graph of arctan look?

facts: The function arcsin is the inverse of sin, and arccos is the inverse of cos.
The principal value range for arcsin is negative pi divided by two to pi divided by two.
The domain for all inverse trig functions is negative one to one.
The graph of y = arcsin(x) is an odd function, meaning it has symmetry about the origin.

quiz.say: What is the value of arccos of one divided by two?
quiz.why: The angle whose cosine is one divided by two, within the principal range, is pi divided by three.

wrong.0: This incorrectly squares the angle value instead of providing the angle itself.
wrong.2: This is the answer for arcsin of one divided by two, confusing the two functions.
wrong.3: Zero is the cosine of zero, but the question asks for the specific angle.

quiz.say: If the domain of a function is restricted to [0, pi], which function is it most likely to be?
quiz.why: The principal value range for arccos is zero to pi, matching the given domain restriction.

wrong.1: The range for arcsin is negative pi divided by two to pi divided by two, not zero to pi.
wrong.2: The range for arctan is negative pi divided by two to pi divided by two, which excludes pi.
wrong.3: Secant is not a standard inverse function with this specific range.

quiz.say: What is the value of arctan of one?
quiz.why: The angle whose tangent is one, within the principal range, is pi divided by four.

wrong.0: This confuses the ratio value with the angle measure in radians.
wrong.1: Pi divided by two is an asymptote, not the value for tangent of one.
wrong.2: This incorrectly multiplies the correct answer by two.
